title: Grants, radio generator deal and veterans crosswalk referral
subtitle: Growth phasing consultant, Belwood Hall funding, farm drainage rezoning hearing, and Strathallan Park update.
overview: Council approved an application to the Rural Ontario Development Program for the maximum available funding for the Belwood Hall renovation, which covers washroom, entrance and main hall upgrades. It also approved a single source contract with Watson and Associates Economists for a growth phasing strategy and a review of commercial land needs, with an in-year top-up from the Corporate DC Reserve Fund of up to $29,000.

Council authorized the CAO to sign an agreement with The Grand 101 FM. The Township will fund a backup generator for the station's transmitter. In return it gets dedicated airtime, including emergency notification access. A request to repaint crosswalks near the Fergus and Elora cenotaphs to honour veterans was referred to the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee.

Council also held a public meeting on a rezoning for 6949 Wellington Road 7 to allow a farm drainage equipment shop. No decision was made, and the by-law will return at a later meeting. The mayor reported that the Township received a grant toward a secondary plan, announced at the meeting. Consent items, including appointments to the Elora BIA board and the Strathallan Park surplus rescission, passed together.

decisions.detail: Council approved applying to the Rural Ontario Development Program for the maximum available funding for the Belwood Hall renovation {{vote:m3}}.
Council awarded Watson and Associates Economists a single source contract for a growth phasing strategy and commercial land review, with up to $29,000 from the Corporate DC Reserve Fund {{vote:m4}}.
Council delegated authority to the CAO to sign an agreement funding a generator at the radio transmitter site in exchange for dedicated airtime {{vote:m5}}.
Council referred the request to repaint crosswalks near the Fergus and Elora cenotaphs to the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee {{vote:m1}}.

Council approved consent items 8.1 to 8.8, including the Elora BIA board appointments, fence-viewer appointments, a Belwood toll booth fundraiser and rescinding the Strathallan Park surplus declaration {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Administrative penalties, toll booth and BIA by-laws
decisions.detail: Council passed by-laws 2025-50 to 2025-52 on screening and hearing officers for the administrative monetary penalty system, the toll booth fundraiser and Elora BIA board appointments {{vote:m6}}.

debate: On the farm drainage rezoning, the applicant's consultant said the shop would serve the business's own equipment, not repair for others. The fuel on site would be for the business's own use and not for sale. A resident of Alma asked about notice to Alma and the neighbouring township, risks to private wells, drainage, and the type and quantity of fuel stored. The consultant said a written response would follow, and staff said the neighbouring township had been circulated.

On the veterans crosswalks, a delegate said the Legions wanted the painting done by November and were still collecting cost figures. Councillors asked about cost, locations and whether one site was on a provincial highway, and about the delay. Staff said the Township has no crosswalk painting policy and that eight weeks was a tight timeline. They noted the DEI committee was already working on recognition policies.

Council discussed whether to refer the crosswalk request to the DEI committee or have staff work with the delegates first. One councillor raised duplicating work, and another suggested including the Belwood Legion. Referral was seen as the most efficient route.

On the Watson single source award, two councillors accepted the rationale but cautioned against relying repeatedly on the same supplier. They said other firms might bring fresh perspectives, and one noted that provincial scrutiny of sole sourcing requires strong supporting data.

On the radio generator, staff said the agreement locks in airtime rates for ten years and gives the Township emergency notification access. The Township would borrow from reserves and repay through its communications budget. A councillor asked who pays legal fees, and staff expected the Township to cover the cost of drafting the agreement.
